q: The satirical work 'Gulliver's Travels' was written by:
e: Gulliver's Travels (1726), a satire on human nature and politics told through voyages to lands like Lilliput, was written by the Irish author Jonathan Swift.

q: The Gothic novel 'Frankenstein' was written by:
e: Frankenstein (1818), the Gothic novel about Victor Frankenstein and the creature he creates, was written by Mary Shelley.

q: The Railway Accidents Review Committee of 1968 was chaired by:
e: The Railway Accidents Inquiry Committee of 1968 was chaired by Justice K. N. Wanchoo, former Chief Justice of India; it followed the Kunzru Committee of 1962 in reviewing railway safety.

q: The Railway Accidents Inquiry Committee of 1978 was chaired by:
e: The Railway Accidents Enquiry Committee of 1978 was chaired by S. M. Sikri, former Chief Justice of India, after two serious accidents in late 1977.

q: The committee appointed in the 1990s to examine the organisational structure and restructuring of Indian Railways was chaired by:
e: The Prakash Tandon Committee (1994) examined the organisational structure of Indian Railways and recommended restructuring and corporatisation of its activities.

q: The Sachar Committee (2006) was appointed to study the:

options.A: Working of the public distribution system
options.C: Social, economic and educational status of the Muslim community in India

e: The Sachar Committee, headed by Justice Rajinder Sachar and reporting in 2006, studied the social, economic and educational status of the Muslim community in India.

q: The Tendulkar Committee (2009) is best known for its recommendations on the:

options.A: Estimation of black money in the economy
options.B: Methodology for the estimation of poverty in India
options.C: Reform of the public sector banks

e: The Tendulkar Committee (2009), chaired by Suresh Tendulkar, revised the methodology for estimating poverty in India, moving beyond a calorie-only norm.

q: The Malhotra Committee (1994) recommended reforms in the:
e: The Malhotra Committee (1994), chaired by former RBI Governor R. N. Malhotra, recommended reforms and liberalisation of the insurance sector, leading to the creation of IRDA.

q: The Tarapore Committee is associated with:

options.A: Convertibility of the rupee on the capital account
options.B: Reforms of the cooperative banking sector

e: The Tarapore Committee (1997 and 2006) laid down a roadmap for convertibility of the rupee on the capital account, that is, fuller capital account convertibility.

q: The Nanavati Commission was appointed to inquire into the:
e: The Nanavati Commission, headed by Justice G. T. Nanavati, inquired into the anti-Sikh riots that followed the assassination of Indira Gandhi in Delhi in 1984.

q: The Srikrishna Commission was appointed to inquire into the:
e: The Srikrishna Commission, headed by Justice B. N. Srikrishna, inquired into the Bombay communal riots of December 1992 and January 1993 and the March 1993 blasts.

q: The Liberhan Commission was appointed to inquire into the:

options.D: Demolition of the Babri Masjid at Ayodhya in 1992

e: The Liberhan Commission, headed by Justice Manmohan Singh Liberhan, inquired into the demolition of the Babri Masjid at Ayodhya on 6 December 1992.

q: The Justice Lodha Committee, appointed by the Supreme Court, recommended reforms in the:

options.A: Administration of cricket in India by the BCCI
options.B: Functioning of the Medical Council of India

e: The Justice R. M. Lodha Committee, appointed by the Supreme Court in 2015, recommended sweeping reforms in the administration of cricket by the BCCI.

q: Kanha National Park, famous for its tigers and barasingha, is located in the State of:
e: Kanha National Park, known for tigers and its population of hard-ground barasingha (swamp deer), is located in the Mandla and Balaghat districts of Madhya Pradesh.

q: Hemis National Park, among the largest national parks of India and home to the snow leopard, is located in:
e: Hemis National Park, one of India's largest national parks and a prime habitat of the snow leopard, is located in Ladakh, east of Leh.

q: Anamudi, the highest peak of South India, is located in the State of:
e: Anamudi, at about 2,695 metres the highest peak in South India and the Western Ghats, is located in Kerala, in the Eravikulam region of Idukki district.

q: The Nohkalikai Falls, among the tallest plunge waterfalls of India, are located in the State of:
e: The Nohkalikai Falls near Cherrapunji, among India's tallest plunge waterfalls at about 340 metres, are located in the East Khasi Hills of Meghalaya.

q: In the Battle of Chandawar (1194), Muhammad Ghori defeated the ruler of Kannauj, namely:
e: In the Battle of Chandawar (1194), Muhammad Ghori defeated Jaichandra, the Gahadavala ruler of Kannauj, opening the way for Turkish rule in the Gangetic plain.

q: The Hawa Mahal, the famous palace of windows, is located in the city of:
e: The Hawa Mahal, the five-storey palace with 953 small windows built by Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh in 1799, is located in Jaipur, Rajasthan.

q: The phonograph, an early device for recording and reproducing sound, was invented by:
e: The phonograph, the first practical device for recording and reproducing sound using a grooved cylinder, was invented by Thomas Alva Edison in 1877.

q: The transistor, the basic building block of modern electronics, was invented at Bell Laboratories by:

options.D: John Bardeen, Walter Brattain and William Shockley

e: The transistor was invented at Bell Laboratories in 1947 by John Bardeen, Walter Brattain and William Shockley, who later shared the Nobel Prize for it.

q: A voltmeter is an instrument used to measure:

options.A: Electric potential difference between two points

e: A voltmeter is connected in parallel in a circuit and measures the electric potential difference, or voltage, between two points.

q: A sextant is an instrument used by navigators primarily to measure:

options.A: The depth of the sea beneath a ship
options.B: The angular altitude of a celestial body above the horizon
options.C: The speed of a ship through water

e: A sextant measures the angle between a celestial body such as the sun or a star and the horizon, allowing navigators to fix their position at sea.

q: A rain gauge is an instrument used to measure:

options.C: The amount of rainfall at a place

e: A rain gauge is an instrument that collects and measures the amount of rainfall at a place over a period of time, usually in millimetres.

q: The first Indian woman to swim across the English Channel was:
e: Arati Saha was the first Indian woman to swim across the English Channel, which she achieved in 1959; she was also the first Indian woman to receive the Padma Shri.

q: The first woman officer of the Indian Administrative Service (IAS) in India was:
e: Anna Rajam George (later Anna Rajam Malhotra), who joined the Indian Administrative Service in 1951, was the first woman IAS officer of India.

q: The first Indian to receive the Ramon Magsaysay Award was:
e: Acharya Vinoba Bhave, the Bhoodan movement leader, was the first Indian to receive the Ramon Magsaysay Award, in 1958.

q: The first Commonwealth Games, held in 1930 as the British Empire Games, were hosted by the city of:
e: The first Commonwealth Games, held in 1930 as the British Empire Games, were hosted by Hamilton in Canada.

q: The capital of Australia is:
e: Canberra is the capital of Australia, chosen as a compromise between the rival cities of Sydney and Melbourne and made the seat of government in 1927.

q: The Strait of Gibraltar connects the Atlantic Ocean with the:
e: The Strait of Gibraltar, between Spain and Morocco, connects the Atlantic Ocean with the Mediterranean Sea.

q: Railway Energy Management Company Limited (REMCL), the nodal agency for power procurement and renewable energy projects of Indian Railways, is a joint venture of RITES Limited with the:

options.D: Power Grid Corporation of India Limited

e: Railway Energy Management Company Limited (REMCL) is a joint venture of RITES Limited and the Ministry of Railways (Indian Railways), set up for power procurement and renewable energy projects of the Railways.

q: The Research Designs and Standards Organisation (RDSO) became the first institution in India to be recognised as a Standard Developing Organisation (SDO) under the 'One Nation One Standard' mission of the:

options.C: National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories

e: RDSO was recognised as a Standard Developing Organisation under the One Nation One Standard mission of the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS), the first institution in India to get this recognition.

q: On the closure of the Indian Railway Stations Development Corporation (IRSDC) in 2021, the station redevelopment projects handled by it were transferred to the:
e: When IRSDC was closed in October 2021, the Railway Board ordered that the stations and station redevelopment projects it managed be handed over to the respective zonal railways.

q: RailTel Corporation of India Limited was conferred the 'Navratna' status by the Government of India in the year:
e: RailTel Corporation of India Limited was conferred Navratna status by the Government of India in 2024, giving its board greater financial and operational autonomy.

q: The headquarters of Braithwaite and Company Limited, a public sector undertaking under the Ministry of Railways, is located at:
e: Braithwaite and Company Limited, a railway PSU known for wagons and cranes, has its headquarters at Kolkata, West Bengal.

q: The corporate headquarters of the Mumbai Railway Vikas Corporation Limited (MRVC) is located at:
e: The Mumbai Railway Vikas Corporation Limited (MRVC), which plans and implements Mumbai suburban railway projects under MUTP, has its corporate headquarters at Mumbai.

q: At the zonal level, the recruitment to Level-1 posts (erstwhile Group 'D') of Indian Railways is conducted through the:
e: At the zonal level, recruitment to Level-1 (erstwhile Group D) posts is conducted through the Railway Recruitment Cells (RRCs) of the zonal railways, unlike Group C recruitment by the RRBs.

q: The Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited (DFCCIL) was incorporated as a special purpose vehicle under the Ministry of Railways in the year:
e: The Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited (DFCCIL) was incorporated in 2006 as a special purpose vehicle under the Ministry of Railways to build dedicated freight corridors.

q: BEML Limited, which manufactures railway coaches and metro cars, has its registered office and headquarters at:
e: BEML Limited, which builds railway coaches, metro cars and defence and mining equipment, has its registered office and headquarters at Bengaluru, Karnataka.

q: Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya at Vadodara, India's first university for the transport and logistics sector, functions as a Central University under the:

options.C: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways

e: Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya at Vadodara, set up for the transport and logistics sector, is a Central University functioning under the Ministry of Railways.

q: Braithwaite, Burn and Jessop Construction Company Limited (BBJ), a public sector undertaking under the Ministry of Railways, is mainly engaged in the:

options.C: Construction of steel bridges and steel structures

e: Braithwaite, Burn and Jessop Construction Company Limited (BBJ) is mainly engaged in the construction of steel bridges, steel structures and foundation work.

q: The Western Dedicated Freight Corridor is being implemented mainly with financial assistance from the:
e: The Western Dedicated Freight Corridor, from Dadri to Jawaharlal Nehru Port, is being implemented mainly with a loan from the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA).

q: The Eastern Dedicated Freight Corridor is being implemented mainly with financial assistance from the:
e: The Eastern Dedicated Freight Corridor, from Ludhiana to Sonnagar and Dankuni, is being implemented mainly with financial assistance from the World Bank.

q: Lucknow city is the headquarters of railway divisions belonging to which two zonal railways?

options.A: Northern Railway and North Central Railway
options.B: North Eastern Railway and East Central Railway
options.C: Northern Railway and North Eastern Railway
options.D: North Central Railway and North Eastern Railway

e: Lucknow hosts division headquarters of two zones: the Lucknow division of Northern Railway (at Charbagh) and the Lucknow division of North Eastern Railway.

q: The Bhawani Mandi railway station is unique because its platform lies partly in Rajasthan and partly in:
e: Bhawani Mandi station in Jhalawar district is unique because the station and platform area straddle the border, lying partly in Rajasthan and partly in Madhya Pradesh.

q: The South Western Railway was formed in 2003 by combining the Hubballi division of South Central Railway with the Bengaluru and Mysuru divisions taken from the:
e: South Western Railway, formed on 1 April 2003, took its Bengaluru and Mysuru divisions from Southern Railway and the Hubballi division from South Central Railway.

q: The Metro Railway, Kolkata was given the status of a zonal railway of Indian Railways, as its 17th zone, in the year:
e: Metro Railway, Kolkata, India's first metro system, was declared the 17th zonal railway of Indian Railways in 2010.

q: The locomotive factory at Dahod in Gujarat, developed with Siemens Mobility, has been set up to manufacture:
e: The locomotive factory at Dahod in Gujarat, set up with Siemens Mobility, manufactures 9,000 HP electric freight locomotives for Indian Railways.

q: The WDG-4G diesel-electric freight locomotives manufactured at the Marhowra factory in Bihar have a power output of:
e: The WDG-4G diesel-electric freight locomotives built at Marhowra in Bihar, based on GE technology, have a power output of 4,500 HP.

q: The National Academy of Indian Railways at Vadodara is housed in the historic palace campus known as:
e: The National Academy of Indian Railways at Vadodara, the apex training institute for railway officers, is housed in the Pratap Vilas Palace campus.

q: The Parel Carriage and Wagon Workshop, located in Mumbai, belongs to which zonal railway?
e: The Parel Carriage and Wagon Workshop in Mumbai, which does periodic overhaul of coaches and wagons, belongs to Central Railway.

q: The historic Loco Workshop and Carriage and Wagon Workshop at Ajmer function under which zonal railway?
e: The historic Loco Workshop and Carriage and Wagon Workshop at Ajmer function under North Western Railway, which has its headquarters at Jaipur.

q: The Rail Wheel Plant at Bela is located in which district of Bihar?
e: The Rail Wheel Plant at Bela, which produces forged wheels for Indian Railways, is located in the Saran district of Bihar, near Chhapra.

q: Which station is regarded as the easternmost railway station of Indian Railways?
e: Ledo station in Assam, terminus of the line beyond New Tinsukia, is regarded as the easternmost railway station of Indian Railways.

q: In workshop accounts of Indian Railways, the abbreviation 'WMS' stands for:
e: In workshop accounts, WMS stands for Workshop Manufacturing Suspense, the suspense head under which the cost of workshop manufacturing jobs is collected.

q: In Indian Railways, the programme 'RSP', under which new locomotives, coaches and wagons are acquired, stands for:
e: RSP stands for Rolling Stock Programme, the programme under which Indian Railways acquires new locomotives, coaches and wagons.

q: The full form of IRSME, an organised Group 'A' service of Indian Railways, is:

options.A: Indian Railway Service of Mechanical Engineers
options.B: Indian Railway Stores and Mechanical Establishment
options.C: Indian Railway Signal and Mechanical Engineers
options.D: Indian Railway Service of Materials Engineers

e: IRSME stands for Indian Railway Service of Mechanical Engineers, the organised Group A service responsible for rolling stock and mechanical engineering.

q: In the classification of railway accounts, the abbreviation 'PU' stands for:
e: In the classification of railway accounts, PU stands for Primary Unit, the basic unit of expenditure classification to which allocations and bookings are made.

q: In the context of retirement benefits of railway employees, the abbreviation 'DCRG' stands for:
e: DCRG stands for Death-cum-Retirement Gratuity, the gratuity payable on retirement or on death while in service under the retirement benefit rules.

q: In railway establishment rules, the leave denoted by 'LAP' stands for:
e: LAP stands for Leave on Average Pay, the earned leave credited to a railway employee at 30 days per year under the leave rules.

q: In railway establishment rules, the grant denoted by 'CTG', paid to an employee on transfer, stands for:
e: CTG stands for Composite Transfer Grant, the grant paid to an employee on transfer involving a change of station to meet relocation expenses.

q: In Government procurement, the portal 'GeM', widely used for stores purchases, stands for:
e: GeM stands for Government e-Marketplace, the national online portal for procurement of goods and services by Government departments and PSUs.

q: In railway works and stores contracts, the abbreviation 'GCC' stands for:
e: GCC stands for General Conditions of Contract, the standard conditions governing railway works and stores contracts.

q: In railway accident relief operations, the abbreviation 'SPART' stands for:
e: SPART stands for Self Propelled Accident Relief Train, a self-propelled train kept ready with equipment and staff for accident relief and rescue work.

q: The full form of IRPFS, the organised Group 'A' service for gazetted officers of the Railway Protection Force, is:

options.B: Indian Railway Police and Force Service
options.C: Indian Railway Protection and Facilities Service
options.D: Indian Railway Personnel and Force Service

e: IRPFS stands for Indian Railway Protection Force Service, the organised Group A service of gazetted officers of the Railway Protection Force.

q: Which two railway CPSEs were upgraded to 'Navratna' status by the Government of India in March 2025?
e: In March 2025, IRCTC and the Indian Railway Finance Corporation (IRFC) were upgraded to Navratna status, taking the number of Navratna CPSEs to 26.

q: 'Kavach' was adopted by Indian Railways as the National Automatic Train Protection (ATP) system in the year:
e: Kavach, the indigenously developed train collision avoidance system, was adopted by Indian Railways as the National Automatic Train Protection (ATP) system in 2020.

q: The New Pamban Bridge, India's first vertical-lift railway sea bridge constructed by Rail Vikas Nigam Limited, was inaugurated in the year:
e: The New Pamban Bridge, India's first vertical-lift railway sea bridge built by RVNL across the Palk Strait to Rameswaram, was inaugurated in 2025.

q: 'Operation Amanat' of the Railway Protection Force is an initiative for:

options.A: Tracing and returning passengers' lost belongings left behind in trains and at stations
options.C: Rescue of runaway children found at stations
options.D: Action against drug smuggling through trains

e: Operation Amanat is an RPF initiative under which lost belongings of passengers left behind in trains and at stations are traced and returned to their owners.

q: 'Operation Uplabdh' of the Railway Protection Force is directed mainly against:

options.C: Touting and illegal sale of e-tickets

e: Operation Uplabdh is an RPF drive against touting and the illegal sale of e-tickets, targeting persons who book tickets unfairly using multiple or fake identities.

q: The Jhansi railway station of Uttar Pradesh was renamed in 2022 as:
e: Jhansi station in Uttar Pradesh was renamed Veerangana Lakshmibai Railway Station in 2022, after Rani Lakshmibai, the warrior queen of Jhansi.

q: The first Vande Bharat Express of South India, flagged off in November 2022, was introduced between:
e: South India's first Vande Bharat Express, flagged off on 11 November 2022, ran between Chennai Central and Mysuru via Bengaluru.

q: Under the Amrit Bharat Station Scheme, the foundation stone laid in August 2023 covered the redevelopment of how many railway stations across the country?
e: Under the Amrit Bharat Station Scheme, the foundation stone laid in August 2023 covered the redevelopment of 508 railway stations across 27 States and Union Territories.

q: The first State to take up a train under the 'Bharat Gaurav' scheme, by running the Kashi Darshan train in November 2022, was:
e: Karnataka was the first State to take up a train under the Bharat Gaurav scheme, running the Kashi Darshan (Kashi Yatra) train from Bengaluru in November 2022.

q: The upgraded version of the Kavach train protection system, approved by RDSO in July 2024 for wider deployment across the railway network, is known as:
e: Kavach Version 4.0, the upgraded automatic train protection specification approved by RDSO in July 2024, was cleared for wider deployment across the network.

q: The novel 'The Great Gatsby' was written by:
e: The Great Gatsby (1925), a novel of wealth and the American Dream in the Jazz Age, was written by F. Scott Fitzgerald.

q: The novel 'To Kill a Mockingbird' was written by:
e: To Kill a Mockingbird (1960), the Pulitzer Prize winning novel about racial injustice in the American South, was written by Harper Lee.

q: The novel 'The Catcher in the Rye' was written by:
e: The Catcher in the Rye (1951), narrated by the disillusioned teenager Holden Caulfield, was written by J. D. Salinger.

q: The novel 'Moby-Dick' was written by:
e: Moby-Dick (1851), the story of Captain Ahab's obsessive hunt for the white whale, was written by Herman Melville.

q: The novel 'The Old Man and the Sea' was written by:
e: The Old Man and the Sea (1952), about the old fisherman Santiago's struggle with a giant marlin, was written by Ernest Hemingway and helped win him the Nobel Prize.

q: The dystopian novel 'Brave New World' was written by:
e: Brave New World (1932), the dystopian novel of a society controlled through pleasure and conditioning, was written by Aldous Huxley.

q: The thriller novel 'The Da Vinci Code' was written by:
e: The Da Vinci Code (2003), the thriller built around symbols, Leonardo da Vinci and secret societies, was written by Dan Brown.

q: The novel 'The Alchemist' was written by:
e: The Alchemist (1988), the fable of Santiago, an Andalusian shepherd following his personal legend, was written by the Brazilian author Paulo Coelho.

q: The novel 'One Hundred Years of Solitude' was written by:
e: One Hundred Years of Solitude (1967), the landmark magic-realist novel of the Buendia family of Macondo, was written by Gabriel Garcia Marquez.

q: The ancient Greek epic poem 'The Odyssey' was composed by:
e: The Odyssey, the ancient Greek epic of Odysseus's ten-year voyage home after the Trojan War, is attributed to Homer, as is the Iliad.

q: The epic poem 'The Divine Comedy' was written by:
e: The Divine Comedy, the Italian epic poem describing journeys through Hell, Purgatory and Paradise, was written by Dante Alighieri in the early 14th century.

q: The Gothic horror novel 'Dracula' was written by:
e: Dracula (1897), the Gothic horror novel told through letters and diary entries about Count Dracula, was written by Bram Stoker.

q: The novel 'The Picture of Dorian Gray' was written by:
e: The Picture of Dorian Gray (1890), the only novel of its author, a tale of beauty, youth and corruption, was written by Oscar Wilde.

q: The novel 'Little Women' was written by:
e: Little Women (1868), the much-loved novel of the four March sisters growing up in New England, was written by Louisa May Alcott.

q: The book 'The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes' was written by:
e: The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes (1892), a collection of twelve cases of the detective created by its author, was written by Arthur Conan Doyle.

q: The play 'Hamlet' was written by:
e: Hamlet, the tragedy of the Prince of Denmark, is one of the most famous plays of William Shakespeare, written around 1600.

q: 'Becoming', published in 2018, is the memoir of:
e: Becoming, published in 2018, is the memoir of Michelle Obama, former First Lady of the United States, covering her childhood, White House years and public life.

q: The Shah Commission (1977) was appointed to inquire into:

options.C: Excesses committed during the Emergency of 1975-77

e: The Shah Commission, headed by Justice J. C. Shah in 1977, inquired into the excesses committed and misuse of authority during the Emergency of 1975-77.

q: The Kargil Review Committee (1999) was chaired by:
e: The Kargil Review Committee (1999), which examined the events leading to the Kargil conflict and recommended defence reforms, was chaired by K. Subrahmanyam.

q: The Chelliah Committee (1991) recommended reforms in the:
e: The Chelliah Committee (1991), chaired by Raja J. Chelliah, recommended comprehensive reforms of the Indian tax system, including lower rates and a wider base.

q: The Second Administrative Reforms Commission was chaired by:
e: The Second Administrative Reforms Commission, set up in 2005 to suggest reforms of public administration, was chaired by Veerappa Moily.

q: The Dinesh Goswami Committee (1990) is associated with:
e: The Dinesh Goswami Committee (1990) is associated with electoral reforms, having recommended changes in election law and the conduct of elections.

q: The Vohra Committee (1993) is associated with the study of:

options.A: The nexus among criminals, politicians and bureaucrats

e: The Vohra Committee (1993), headed by former Home Secretary N. N. Vohra, studied the nexus among criminals, politicians and bureaucrats in India.

q: The Urjit Patel Committee (2013-14) is associated with reforms in the:
e: The Urjit Patel Committee (2013-14) recommended reforms of the monetary policy framework, including inflation targeting and a monetary policy committee for the RBI.

q: The Nachiket Mor Committee (2013) is associated with:

options.B: Financial inclusion for small businesses and low-income households

e: The Nachiket Mor Committee (2013), set up by the RBI, dealt with comprehensive financial services and financial inclusion for small businesses and low-income households.
